record.tooling: Root access makes this the most chainable option among the storage providers compared: AList, MinIO or a Cloudflare tunnel endpoint can run on the box itself.
record.chaining: Composition with external storage pools is unestablished.
record.limits_note: Bandwidth is a hard counter on these plans. Capacity grows 1 GB per day on the expanding plan series. Billing and ordering systems were offline during testing on 2026-10-21.
record.reliability_note: Canadian provider since 2010, RAIDZ2. Treat as a real but currently-wobbly vendor.

egress.terms: Two options per plan, switchable in the control panel. Option 1 (the one that matters): 'Unlimited transfer — 250 Mbps port, grows +1 Mbps/day up to 1 Gbps'. Option 2: '10 Gbps port — 12TB 1Gbps monthly cap (throttled to ~10 Mbps after cap)'. So the truly unmetered option is speed-clamped at 250 Mbps and slowly ramps, and the fast option is a 12 TB cap that degrades to ~10 Mbps rather than billing overage. The provider states traffic is counted on BOTH directions (LET thread 199994 p9: 'We count traffic from both d[irections]').

record.tooling: rclone SFTP, any backup tool, Xen/KVM root
record.chaining: Root virtual private server supporting AList or MinIO installation. The 250 Mbps unmetered network option provides continuous throughput without monthly byte quotas.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: none. 'Unlimited Expanding Storage' plans add +1 to +15 GB/day of disk rather than granting it up front. Xen on the older storage line.
record.reliability_note: Long-standing CA provider with a strong LowEndTalk record — 'Have been using servarica for close a year now. Absolutely no issues' (thread 180949), 'I just renewed my storage vps with servarica for the 2nd year never had issue'.

free_tier.stated: Shrimp 1: 500 GB base + 1 GB/day automatic growth, $5/mo. I.e. it crosses 1 TB at ~day 500 and 1.87 TB at 4 years, on a fixed price. Shrimp 2: 500 GB + 2 GB/day, $7/mo. Lobster: 2 TB + 3 GB/day, $10/mo. Separate fixed line: Opossum 1 = 1 TB for $29/YEAR, Polar Bear 2 TB $48/yr, Killer Whale 3.5 TB $84/yr.

egress.terms: Includes 12 TB per month (Shrimp) or 18 TB per month (Lobster) on 1 Gbps ports, with metered traffic beyond allowances.

record.tooling: KVM with root. SSH/SFTP/rsync/rclone-sftp. RaidZ2 HDD backend on the fixed line.
record.chaining: The genuinely interesting mechanic: this is 'free storage over time' priced as a subscription. Capacity is a function of tenure, so the chaining move is tenure, not accounts. A $29/year Opossum is 1 TB now and the expanding plans add 365 GB/year for free at fixed price. No free tier.
record.limits_note: Bandwidth is the real cap (12–18 TB/mo). Growth is 1–3 GB/day, so it is unusable for a 20 TB cold archive in year one. It is a decade instrument. Montreal location.
record.reliability_note: Long-running Canadian host with a heavy Black Friday presence on LET/NodeSeek; NodeSeek threads name it among the 'highly trusted' big-disk providers. RaidZ2 on the fixed line.
record.confidence_note: The 2026-11-03 evidence rows read https://servarica.com/unlimited-storage-vps/ (Shrimp 1, Shrimp 2 and Lobster base sizes, daily growth, bandwidth and monthly and yearly prices) and https://servarica.com/storage-servers-2/ (the fixed-size yearly prices). Price and growth that decide the paid-only verdict cite vendor captures; identity is not read from a sign-up page.
